A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same D2C research, despite the changed title and formatting. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated experiments and visualizations.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet generation experiments, comparisons against selection and condensation baselines, component ablations and generated samples in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original ImageNet experiments and adds CIFAR-10 results, scorer and encoder ablations, runtime measurements and a LAION difficulty-score analysis.

M1.justification: Appendix G adds a limited text-to-image adaptation that replaces class conditioning with text conditioning during difficulty scoring. The core class-to-image Select/Attach pipeline, DC-Embedding, visual alignment and training objective remain unchanged. Revisions to the conflicting score and sorting descriptions do not establish an actual redesign of the class-to-image procedure.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates ImageNet-1K class-to-image generation at 256×256 and 512×512. v3 adds CIFAR-10 generation and analyzes LAION text-image pairs scored with SDXL, extending both dataset and conditioning coverage. The LAION experiment reports a difficulty distribution, not trained text-to-image generation performance.

E2.justification: v3 Table 4 adds RDED to the SRe2L comparison on both DiT-L/2 and SiT-L/2. New Table 3 adds REPA-E and REG to the acceleration comparisons and reports additional L-model comparisons with REPA. The Random, K-Center and Herding comparator set in Table 1 is unchanged.

E3.justification: The existing ImageNet budgets, resolutions and documented training defaults are retained. Added experiments introduce a CIFAR-10 protocol with 100 images per class, a 1K training subset and 100k steps, plus alternative scorer and visual-encoder configurations. Recall is removed from the main evaluation description and result tables, although its definition remains in Appendix D. These are bounded protocol additions and reporting changes.

E4.justification: v3 Table 5 expands the component ablation to separate Select and Attach contributions. Tables 6 and 7 add tests of strong, weaker and absent scoring models, computational overhead and visual-encoder robustness. Figure 10 extends the condensation failure examples to RDED. Conversely, v1 Figure 7's additional interval and fixed-mean-loss sampling curves are removed; the other interval analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or error bars. The added experiments do not introduce an uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: New results include RDED gFID values of 166.2 and 97.5, CIFAR-10 gFID of 9.72 for Random versus 3.95 for D2C, and additional component, encoder and runtime results. Table 1 is unchanged, and the 512×512 SiT 300k results already appeared in v1 Appendix J. Recall entries and the removed Figure 7 results disappear. New Table 3 assigns 10k steps to DiT scores 14.81 and 4.2, whereas Table 1 still assigns them 100k; these entries cannot establish a verified same-setting acceleration gain.

T1.justification: Section 3.1 revises the approximate constant-denominator assumption and the mathematical difficulty-score definition. v1 Equation 6's negative-log-of-exponential expression becomes negative expected squared error in v3 Equation 7, and the stated score ordering reverses. The revised equation still conflicts with Algorithm 2's positive mean squared error. These are limited formal revisions, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: Both versions claim the first diffusion dataset-condensation framework, consisting of Select and Attach, and substantial training acceleration with small datasets across architectures and resolutions. The headline 4.3 FID at 40k steps and 100–233× acceleration claims are retained. New supporting experiments and revised research positioning do not materially change these central contributions.

C2.justification: v3 removes v1 Appendix A's explicit acknowledgment that final converged performance does not fully match baseline benchmarks, together with its proposed encoder fine-tuning remedy. It adds interpretations concerning weak or absent scorer viability, encoder robustness, expected text-to-image applicability and why medium-only selection underperforms interval sampling. These materially change the discussion of mechanisms and applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: v3 adds Algorithm 2 specifying frozen-model latent encoding, noise injection and averaging of denoising losses, explains how the existing Medium selection variant is constructed, and provides scoring and training times. Figure 5 also newly specifies the backbone and absence of CFG. Core hyperparameters and hardware disclosures remain substantially unchanged, with no new code or data access information.

R1.justification: The introduction, related work and new Appendix A substantially reposition D2C within image-level condensation through selection and enrichment of real images, broadening v1's synthetic-data optimization framing. New discussion distinguishes D2C from InfoBatch and Pruning then Reweighting and relates it to OD3 and other image-level approaches. References also expand to newer acceleration methods, including REG and REPA-E.

P1.justification: v3 retitles the paper and substantially rewrites the abstract, introduction, related work, scoring explanation and conclusion. It introduces a separate experimental setup subsection and reorganizes the supplementary sections. The limitations and broader-impact sections disappear, while positioning, exploration and acknowledgment sections are added.

P2.justification: The document changes from predominantly single-column to two-column formatting, extensively resizing and relocating figures and tables. v3 consolidates the 512×512 results into the main table, removes Recall columns, expands ablation and baseline tables, adds a scoring algorithm and LAION histogram, and expands the condensation visualization with RDED. Most existing method diagrams and generation galleries are retained rather than newly produced.

improvement.justification: The added component controls, scorer-dependence tests and end-to-end timing analysis address important gaps in v1's efficiency evidence; RDED and CIFAR-10 results also strengthen validation. However, v3 removes Recall results exposing diversity tradeoffs and the explicit final-convergence limitation. Its new acceleration table also introduces conflicting 10k versus 100k training budgets for identical DiT scores. These benefits and losses directly affect the central efficiency and quality claims, preventing a reliable net improvement judgment.
